title: Bitmap 像素数据、Native Heap 与 Graphics 归因
key_conclusions: Bitmap attribution requires separating wrapper retained paths from pixel memory buckets.
Software Bitmaps usually require Native Heap, heapprofd, showmap, and smaps evidence, while hardware Bitmaps require Graphics, dma-buf, and platform buffer evidence.
HPROF proves Java ownership but not pixel storage location.
Acceptance requires wrapper retained paths, Native Heap, Graphics/dma-buf, and decode peak evidence to move consistently.
shallow_points: The article does not include real meminfo, showmap, smaps, HPROF, heapprofd, or dmabuf outputs.
It does not validate hardware Bitmap accounting across devices, Android versions, GPU drivers, and image libraries.
It does not provide a runnable sample generating software, hardware, transformed, and cached Bitmap cases.
It does not include automated delta calculations joining theoretical pixel size with observed memory buckets.
discovered_connections: Day 41's wrapper-versus-pixel split becomes the core attribution workflow.
Day 33's dma-buf producer-consumer model is necessary for hardware Bitmap and Graphics cases.
Day 34's heapprofd workflow can identify software pixel allocations when stack capture is available.
Day 43 should use these attribution rules when explaining inSampleSize and inBitmap decode peak control.
Day 44 should map Glide MemoryCache and BitmapPool to wrapper, Native Heap, and Graphics buckets.
suggest_future_topics: Day 43 should focus on BitmapFactory.Options, inSampleSize, inBitmap, decode temporary memory, and peak reduction.
